query: For high-entropy-alloy multilayer protective coatings, what testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain their resistance to time-dependent plastic deformation? Specify what governs the behavior and why, an unspecified controlled comparison that would reveal it, the expected observations relative to a baseline, applicable boundaries, supporting evidence, and an outcome that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: In Al-Cr-Fe-Ni high-entropy-alloy multilayer coatings, semicoherent interfaces (formed at a 16 nm modulation period) promote stress-induced interfacial amorphization that redistributes local stress and lowers atomic migration barriers, thereby shifting the dominant creep mechanism from dislocation-mediated slip to rate-limited atomic diffusion/interface slip. This transition results in enhanced room-temperature creep resistance compared to coatings with coherent (8 nm) or grain-boundary-dominated (32/80 nm) interfaces.
generation.material_initial_state: As-deposited, approximately 1 μm-thick FCC/BCC Al-Cr-Fe-Ni high-entropy-alloy multilayer coatings produced from Al0.2CrFeNi and Al targets.
generation.intervention: Vary the modulation period (individual layer thickness, λ) among 8, 16, 32, and 80 nm by RF magnetron sputtering to create multilayers with coherent, semicoherent, or grain-boundary-dominated interfaces, then perform room-temperature nanoindentation creep testing.
generation.conditions: Deposition under a base pressure of ~5 × 10^-4 Pa, Ar flow of 100 sccm, working pressure of 0.3 Pa, with power settings of 150 W on the HEA target and alternating 0/30 W on the Al target during a 1 h deposition. Nanoindentation testing at room temperature with a maximum load of 5 mN, loading rates of 1, 0.1, and 0.01 mN/s, a 100 s hold period, and a 20 s unloading period, with indentation depths maintained at approximately 1/10–1/7 of the coating thickness.
generation.structural_mediator: Interface coherency. Specifically, M8 exhibits coherent interfaces with continuous atomic planes, M16 forms semicoherent FCC/BCC interfaces with misfit dislocations, and M32/M80 become dominated by grain boundaries due to the modulation period exceeding the typical ~20 nm grain diameter.
generation.mechanism: Semicoherent interfaces cause dislocation pileup and localized high stress during deformation, which in turn triggers stress-induced interfacial amorphization. The resulting amorphous regions, with their free volume and lower atomic-migration barriers, facilitate creep via atomic diffusion or interface slip, whereas coherent interfaces allow smooth dislocation transmission and grain-boundary dominated structures promote dislocation slip/climb.
generation.predicted_outcome: The 16 nm (M16) semicoherent multilayer will exhibit the highest room-temperature creep resistance and a transition in the creep mechanism as indicated by a lower creep stress exponent (approaching 1–2, consistent with diffusion/interface-slip creep) relative to the 8 nm (M8) and 32/80 nm (M32/M80) samples that show higher stress exponents indicative of dislocation-mediated creep.
generation.baseline: Creep behavior in M8 (λ = 8 nm, coherent interfaces) and M32/M80 (λ = 32/80 nm, grain-boundary-dominated interfaces) where deformation is predominantly dislocation-mediated.
generation.boundary: Findings are applicable for sputtered ~1 μm-thick FCC/BCC Al-Cr-Fe-Ni multilayers tested under room-temperature nanoindentation creep conditions with maximum loads of 5 mN and loading rates ranging from 1 to 0.01 mN/s. The hypothesis may not hold at elevated temperatures or under macroscopic creep conditions.
generation.uncertainty: There is uncertainty regarding the direct observation and quantification of stress-induced interfacial amorphization, as previous MD and HRTEM studies suggest its occurrence but do not conclusively establish its prevalence or precise role in the deformation mechanism.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare multilayer coatings with modulation periods of 8, 16, 32, and 80 nm under the specified deposition conditions. Characterize the interfaces using XRD and TEM/IFFT to confirm the type (coherent, semicoherent, or grain-boundary dominated). Conduct nanoindentation creep tests at the specified loading rates and record load–displacement and creep displacement during the hold period. Analyze the data by plotting ln(strain rate) versus ln(flow stress) to obtain the creep stress exponent (n) for each sample.
measurements: XRD to determine phase constituents and detect signatures of amorphization.
TEM/IFFT to distinguish between coherent and semicoherent interfaces and to identify any amorphous interfacial regions.
Nanoindentation load–displacement curves to measure creep displacement over time.
Calculation of the creep stress exponent (n) from ln(strain rate) versus ln(flow stress) plots.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the 16 nm multilayer does not exhibit a significantly lower creep stress exponent (indicative of a shift to atomic diffusion/interface-slip-mediated creep) and enhanced creep resistance relative to both the 8 nm and 32/80 nm samples, the hypothesis is rejected.
